description:
Listed Building Consent for the retention and refurbishment of the Grade ll listed 129-130 High Street, including: the retention and repair of the High Street facade, party walls and second floor; the part-retention of the first floor, with a section to be raised by 320mm to remove an internal step; the re-modelling of the rear elevation in line with the face of the existing outrigger; the retention of the staircase above ground floor level; the retention of internal partitions where possible; 
The recording, removal, repair and reinforcement of internal partitions where necessary to allow reinstatement at a higher level; the retention of fireplaces, Victorian shopfront, tiled entrance thresholds and chimneys, or careful dismantling and reassembly in their original form where necessary

Condition : 3 - Details in respect of the following shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority before the relevant work is begun. The relevant work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

A)	Drawings at 1:5 with details of glazing bars at 1:1 of proposed new windows.

Condition : 4 - A schedule of repair shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority before the relevant work is begun. The relevant work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Condition : 5 - All new internal and external works, including works of making good for the retained fabric, shall match the original work in type, colour, texture, profile and dimensions of materials and in detailed execution, including facebond and pointing.

Condition : 6 - No new plumbing, pipes, soil stacks, flues, vents grilles, security alarms or ductwork shall be fixed on the external faces of the building unless shown on the drawings hereby approved.

Condition : 7 - Existing internal decoration features, including fireplaces, windows, staircases, staircase balustrade and other staircase woodwork, shall remain in their existing position where possible, and shall be fully protected during the course of works, except for opening up works and other works required to implement the consent, unless expressly specified in the approved drawings.

For the avoidance of doubt, fixing points for any handrail or railing into any part of the existing building shall be kept at a minimum and shall be made into the mortar joints between the stones using non-ferrous fixings; where this is required, full details of these fixings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Planning Authority prior to any works on site.
Condition : 8 - The existing historic shopfront shall be retained, repaired and fully protected during the course of works on site unless expressly specified in the approved drawings.

Condition : 9 - No demolition works of the existing buildings shall commence on site until an appropriate programme of building recording (including architectural/historical analysis and photography) has been carried out in respect of the buildings to be demolished and submitted to and agreed in writing by the local planning authority. This record shall be carried out by an archaeologist/building recorder/organisation with acknowledged experience in the recording of standing buildings, the identity of whom shall first have been agreed with the local planning authority and is in accordance with the advice in Historic England's: Understanding Historic Buildings- A Guide to Good Recording Practice. The recording shall be carried out in accordance with a written specification, and presented in a form and to a timetable, which shall first have been agreed in writing with the local planning authority. 
Once agreed any demolition shall be carried out by hand [or using hand-held tools] only and the materials stored for re-use.
Condition : 10 - The re-wiring and fitting of new light fittings shall make use of existing service channels in the fabric and no new service channels shall be chased into historic fabric.

Condition : 11 - Before the walls of the development hereby permitted are constructed, a specification for a lime based mortar (sample to be provided) to be used for the repointing shall first be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, alongside a sample panel of the stonework/brickwork and mortar finish proposed, measuring one square metre in area, which shall be constructed on site for the written approval of the local planning authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details.

Condition : 12 - Prior to their installation details of all new or replacement rainwater goods (which shall be of metal construction and finished in black) and their means of fixing to the building shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
